w: A lighthouse with no sea in sight: this 102-metre tower rises from Parque Sarmiento purely as a symbol, unveiled with Cordoba's governor Juan Schiaretti on hand to declare it a new icon for the city. There's no coastline for hundreds of kilometres inland here - just a landlocked beacon standing in for one.
s: A 102-metre lighthouse with no sea nearby
_facts: Lighthouse-like monument, not a functioning navigational lighthouse
Opened with Governor Juan Schiaretti attending, intended as a city icon

n: Marquis of Sobremonte provincial historical museum
w: This house museum takes its name from Rafael de Sobremonte, 3rd Marquis of Sobremonte, who lived here while running the administration of colonial Cordoba during the 18th century. It's now the city's provincial historical museum, housed in the same walls its Spanish-era namesake once occupied.
s: Colonial governor's house, now a history museum
_facts: Named after Rafael de Sobremonte, 3rd Marquis of Sobremonte
He lived in the building while administering colonial Cordoba in the 18th century
Now the city's provincial historical museum
_sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquis of Sobremonte provincial historical museum
